reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it teaches viewers how slippage tolerance works on decentralized exchanges using a concrete croissant-price example and an on-screen PancakeSwap demonstration. It explains that higher tolerance can increase execution speed but may cause the buyer to pay more, and recommends finding a compromise rather than promising profit or requesting a transfer of money or personal data. The description includes an exchange referral link, but the supplied content does not establish deceptive claims or harmful destination behavior.

citations.quote: What is the Slippage? Understand why adjust the Slippage on Pancakeswap, Uniswap, Sushiiswap
the slippage is the difference between the price at which you want to cross your order and the price of the market you want to pay when your order is executed
The goal is to find the right compromise between speed and value

opening.argument: The video supplies a direct reward-and-action pathway: viewers without an account are told to create one, and the speaker links that action to receiving 10% on future transactions through the supplied link. That is not merely neutral education; it is a concrete transaction benefit attached to registration and referral use. The promised benefit is easy to understand and requires a financial-platform action, fitting a low-barrier acquisition incentive even though the surrounding discussion is instructional.

citations.quote: If you don't have an account yet do not hesitate to create one. Registration is free.
Then thanks to my link, you will have 10% on your future transactions, this is the maximum that I can donate you
https://accounts.binance.com/fr/ Recording?ref=KSC446TB

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content educational overlooks the separate, explicit solicitation in the description. The tutorial context makes the referral more effective because viewers are already being shown how to transact in crypto. The fact that registration is free does not remove the linked benefit, and the disclaimer does not negate that viewers are directed to an external account-creation route promising 10% on future transactions.

citations.quote: If you don't have an account yet do not hesitate to create one. Registration is free.
you will have 10% on your future transactions
When you want to buy Cryptos, say SafeMoon for example

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows a disclosed referral incentive, not an implausible giveaway or asset claim. It does not establish that the benefit is deceptive, unavailable, or harmful, and the video expressly warns that viewers can lose all their capital. A one-level account referral attached to an otherwise instructional explanation is insufficient to show a scam acquisition flow.

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals converge around a viewer action. The description promotes crypto participation and directs viewers to create an account through a referral link for 10% on future transactions. The demonstration then shows a token swap interface with 12% slippage tolerance and an “Unlock Wallet” control, while the explanation says that tolerance can mean paying 12% more. Even if the presentation uses technical language, this is a high-consequence acquisition path paired with an attractive transaction benefit and a wallet-related next step.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. The issue is their combination: crypto purchasing, a referral destination, a stated 10% future-transaction benefit, and a displayed wallet-unlock step. The speaker also normalizes materially higher payment tolerance, so viewers are not merely reading a definition; they are being guided toward a consequential transaction while an incentive encourages platform participation.

citations.quote: we are ready to pay 12% more
you will have 10% on your future transactions

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not establish a low-barrier scam. The 12% figure is presented as slippage tolerance, explicitly describing a possible higher execution price rather than a promised reward. The wallet button is part of the displayed exchange interface, and the referral is openly disclosed. The speaker also explains that higher slippage means paying more, which is a risk warning rather than concealment.

opening.argument: Although framed as a lesson about slippage, the presentation also functions as promotion for crypto participation. The title names several exchanges, the spoken example centers on buying SafeMoon, the screen demonstrates a BNB-to-SAFEMOON swap, and the description lists many additional tokens before directing viewers to create an account through a referral link for a future-transaction benefit. The instructional framing therefore doubles as a practical funnel: viewers learn the mechanism while being steered toward a platform and token-purchase workflow.

Viewers are shown a specific crypto exchange workflow and then offered a referral-linked benefit for creating an account. The warning language may sound cautious, but it accompanies rather than replaces a concrete direction toward participation and a promised transaction advantage.
